description: Structural probe corpus for complex English. target_frame lists required English slot heads (not exact fon). Probes with status pass gate CI via --assert; broken probes track known gaps.

phrases.en: I want to go to the city but I am afraid of the dark.
phrases.note: but-clause split; want omitted per golden L13 (no obligation grammar)

phrases.en: They ran toward us from the river.
phrases.note: compound path toward + from

phrases.en: The hunter followed the animal into the forest.
phrases.note: transitive motion + into path

phrases.en: Are you going to the market tomorrow?
phrases.note: question subject preserved; tomorrow trailing time

phrases.en: The child ran away when the dog barked.
phrases.note: subordinate when-clause not yet split

phrases.en: Go away and leave me alone.
phrases.note: coordinated motion clauses

phrases.en: Come here quickly.
phrases.note: deictic here landmark

phrases.en: We should not go there at night.
phrases.note: negation on motion frame

phrases.en: I am going to tell you a story about the old king.
phrases.note: going-to-VERB future + speech event

phrases.en: The bird flew over the lake and landed near the trees.
phrases.note: over path; second clause partial

phrases.en: Bring the water from the spring to the camp.
phrases.note: bring not in lexicon; dual paths incomplete

phrases.en: He said he would return home after the sun set.
phrases.note: reported speech + temporal after

phrases.en: I have never been to the city before.
phrases.note: perfect aspect collapsed; city landmark

phrases.en: When she arrives, we will leave for the mountains.
phrases.note: when opens clause; arrives gap

phrases.en: I go to the city.
phrases.note: regression guard from level 12

phrases.en: I want to eat seafood.
phrases.note: desire+infinitive frame; seafood transparent assembly

phrases.en: I want to eat sea food.
phrases.note: sea food token merge converges with seafood

phrases.en: seafood
phrases.note: word mode; must not collapse to eat

phrases.en: I want to sleep.
phrases.note: desire+infinitive: event desire + object infinitive verb

phrases.en: Do not eat the fish.
phrases.note: imperative negation; fish must not hypernym-collapse to eat

phrases.en: The fish swims in the river.
phrases.note: fish in subject slot must stay fish, not eat

phrases.en: I am afraid of the dark.
phrases.note: emotion predicate + fear object

phrases.en: Nobody went home after dark.
phrases.note: quantifier + temporal after + landmark

phrases.en: Tell the child a story about the sea.
phrases.note: speech event + recipient + topic modifier

phrases.en: We ran through the forest toward the river.
phrases.note: through path + toward path on same motion frame

phrases.en: Bring me water.
phrases.note: bring resolves via la; water object present

phrases.en: No sentience can live inside it.
phrases.note: abstract 'sentience' composes (think+self); negation + inside path

phrases.en: Machines act and do not learn.
phrases.note: 'machine' composes (make+thing) not animal; negation preserved

phrases.en: Consciousness stays outside the system.
phrases.note: consciousness (know+self) + system (all+thing) both compose

phrases.en: Long ago, when the world was young, the animal walked on the earth.
phrases.note: Scene structure: front temporal scene (long_ago/beginning/world) before Actor; ta by Action; no invented negation. Track until golden-stable.

phrases.en: Long ago, when the forest was young, people walked to the river.
phrases.note: Era scene + motion destination; must not invent do/mo scene clauses; scene time fronts before Actor.

phrases.en: Yesterday, before the rain, the child sat near the fire.
phrases.target_frame: before · rain · child · sit · near · fire
phrases.note: Calendar + before-X scene with stative sit; ta by Action; no dummy do.

phrases.en: When the dog barked, the child ran to the house.
phrases.note: Real subordinate with its own actor+action → discourse split (two frames), not time+do mini-clauses.

phrases.en: Tomorrow, after the sun, we will go to the water.
phrases.note: Future scene fronting; sa by Action; after+sun as scene time; no dummy do.

phrases.en: Why are you here?
phrases.note: why probe = nohu gak (unknown + cause dimension). Interrogative coverage: the golden corpus has levels for what/who/where/when but none for why, so these probes are the only regression guard.

phrases.en: Why did you go?
phrases.note: why on a bare motion frame; keeps actor and past ta

phrases.en: Why do you want the water?
phrases.note: why on a desire frame; must not displace the want event

phrases.en: Why is the child afraid?
phrases.note: why on an emotion predicate; no dummy do invented

phrases.en: Why did you take the water?
phrases.note: why on a transitive frame; probe survives alongside object

phrases.en: Why did you go to the river?
phrases.note: Pre-existing WH loss, not specific to why: when a content question also carries a destination path, the WH word is dropped and unresolved[] stays EMPTY, so the loss is silent. 'Where did you go to the river?' drops where identically, which is how this was isolated. Tracked here because a silently dropped question word is worse than an honest gap.

phrases.en: How many animals do you own?
phrases.note: Quantity probe has no dimension root to pair with, so how_many is an honest gap (RN-37). Must NOT regress to nohu lek: lek is a value on the scale, not the scale. Frame heads name the dimension this needs, so this probe stays broken until one exists.

phrases.en: How do you make fire?
phrases.note: No neutral way/manner/method concept. Must NOT regress to nohu ha: rule (ha) is prescriptive, not manner.

phrases.en: Are you tired or sick?
phrases.note: Disjunction IS expressible as of the lu rule and the LLM path renders be nes femtam du lu. This probe stays broken because probes run translateEnglish, which aliases the deprecated rule-based engine: it scatters the alternatives into event=[tired] and object=[sick] instead of grouping them, so there is no coordinated group to mark. Blocked on the rule-based engine grouping coordinated items, not on the disjunction rule.

phrases.en: Do you want food or water?
phrases.note: Same rule-based grouping gap. Renders identically to 'Do you want food and water?' (be sak tel ye), which is the and/or conflation the lu rule exists to remove. Guards against the two ever being indistinguishable again once grouping lands.

phrases.en: Is the baby a girl or boy?
phrases.note: Not a disjunction failure: girl and boy have no roots, so both alternatives drop upstream and there is nothing for lu to attach to. Correctly reports gaps [girl, boy] rather than marking a single item. Lexical gap, tracked separately from the coordination rule.

phrases.en: Do you mean this or that?
phrases.note: Alternatives are demonstratives, which SKIP discards as function words, so both drop and or stays an honest gap. Needs demonstrative support, not coordination work.
